name: Miriam
bio:
Miriam is the daughter of Amram and Jochebed, the elder sister of Moses and Aaron, and one of the women in Scripture specifically called a "prophetess" (Exodus 15:20). When the infant Moses was set adrift on the Nile in a basket, it was Miriam who watched from a distance, and after Pharaoh's daughter discovered the baby, she cleverly stepped forward to suggest that Moses' own mother serve as his nurse — allowing him to be raised under his birth mother's care (Exodus 2:4-8).

After Israel crossed the Red Sea and escaped the pursuing Egyptians, Miriam took up a timbrel and led the women in dancing, singing, "Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea" — one of the earliest recorded scenes of a woman leading worship in Scripture (Exodus 15:20-21).

During the wilderness journey, Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses over the Cushite woman he had married, asking, "Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?" The LORD appeared to them and rebuked them for daring to speak against His servant Moses, who was faithful in all His house and spoke with God face to face; when the cloud departed from the tabernacle, Miriam was struck with leprosy, white as snow. Aaron pleaded with Moses on her behalf, and Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days before being restored (Numbers 12). In her later years, Miriam died and was buried in the wilderness of Zin at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1), closing out a life spent alongside her two brothers leading Israel's people out of Egypt and through the wilderness.
